shared_refusal_classes.description: The requested capability, intent kind, or operation kind is not recognized by the surface.
The schema version is not supported or the payload fails schema validation.
The request is syntactically or structurally invalid.
The required trace_id is absent from the request.
A duplicate message_id or idempotency key was detected, indicating possible replay.
The payload exceeds the surface's maximum size limit.
The payload contains dangerous content (command injection, escaped paths, env var injection, redaction violation).
The payload contains a raw secret, token, or credential in cleartext.
The payload contains a raw filesystem path that could enable traversal.
The operation requires authentication that is not present or not satisfied.
Credential material (tokens, keys, OAuth codes, JWT assertions) is refused from crossing the surface boundary in v1.
The required tool permission, capability gate, or step-up is not granted.
A required OAuth scope is not granted for the operation.
The target repository, user subject, customer, or resource is not found or not accessible.
Access to the target repository or resource is denied by policy or insufficient permissions.
A mutation operation (write, update, delete) is refused by policy or capability gate.
A destructive or release-affecting mutation is refused in the current version.
A credentialed mutation (requiring provider auth) is refused because live auth is not enabled.
An operation requiring external network access is refused because network is disabled.
Live authentication mechanisms (OAuth, domain-wide delegation) are deferred to a future slice. Refused by default.
Live protocol transport (MCP, ACP, A2A network) is deferred to a future slice. Refused by default.
The method or feature is honestly deferred via NotImplementedMethodError or stub.
The operation was refused due to rate limiting or throttling.
The operation exceeded resource budgets (timeout, server capacity, memory, CPU).
An internal processing error prevented the operation from completing.
A validation check (contract, counterexample, assertion) failed.
A compiler candidate was rejected or quarantined by the validation matrix.
CI evidence is present but some assertions are unverified, placing the verdict on hold.
CI evidence is missing, malformed, or contradictory — the verdict is fail.

surface_mappings.rationale: Bridge refuses intents whose intent_kind is not in the known enum. This is a capability discovery failure.
Bridge rejects messages whose schema_version does not match the expected const. Schema version mismatch is a schema validation failure.
Bridge refuses messages whose envelope kind is not recognized. Same class as unknown_intent_kind — capability not found.
Bridge requires trace_id on every envelope. Absence means the request cannot be traced.
Bridge detects duplicate message_ids as replay attacks or idempotency violations.
Bridge enforces MAX_BYTES_ENVELOPE_BODY. Exceeding it triggers this refusal.
Bridge refuses mutation intents that lack the required capability gate membership. Missing permission, not missing capability ID.
Bridge cannot find a matching capability for the requested operation. Capability does not exist.
Bridge refuses the mutation_class outright — e.g., all credentialled_mutation intents refused in v1.
Bridge refuses provider-credentialled mutations because live provider auth is not enabled in v1.
Mutations that would affect release artifacts are treated as destructive and refused.
Mutations requiring external network are refused because network is disabled in default policy.
Payload contains dangerous patterns (injection, traversal, env injection).
Payload contains raw secret material (tokens, keys) that must never cross the bridge.
Payload contains raw filesystem paths that could enable traversal.
Operation requires authentication that the frontend session does not have.
The capability gate check failed — the tool or operation is not in the allowed gate set.
Bridge enforces per-connection rate limits. Exceeding them triggers this refusal.
Bridge queue or connection pool is full. Server capacity is at its budget limit.
The envelope JSON does not parse or fails basic structural validation. This is malformed input, not schema version mismatch.
The payload violates content-light redaction rules. Classified as unsafe because redacted content may contain dangerous material.
An unexpected internal error occurred during bridge processing.
surface_mappings.notes: Bridge dispatcher emits this when an unhandled exception escapes.

surface_mappings.rationale: SDK run_result with verdict=refused maps to mutation_refused as the default shared class. SDK refusal_code is a free-form string; specific codes would map more narrowly.

MCP refusal at tier levels (tier_3_mutation_refused, tier_4_credentialed_refused, tier_5_destructive_refused) all map through the capability profile. Schema-only; never instantiated at runtime. Default class is permission_missing (tier-based gate).
MCP capability profile declares tier 3 (mutation) operations refused. Maps to mutation_refused.
MCP capability profile declares tier 4 (credentialed) operations refused.
MCP capability profile declares tier 5 (destructive) operations refused.
ACP refusal envelope exists in schema but ACP refusals are raised as NotImplementedMethodError, not as structured envelopes. Schema-only default maps to not_implemented_deferred.
ACP authenticate() and resume_session() raise NotImplementedMethodError. These are honest deferral stubs, not runtime bugs.
surface_mappings.notes: Deferral seam 'acp_live_notimplemented_stubs' classified as alpha_blocker in the convergence review.

surface_mappings.rationale: A2A delegation_receipt refusal_code is a free-form string. Default class is permission_missing (delegation denied).
Metadata read refusal means the repository is not accessible. Resource denial, not capability unknown.
Contents read refusal means the repository is not accessible or the resource is denied.
Branches read refusal means the repository is not accessible.
Commits read refusal means the repository is not accessible.
Issues read refusal means the repository or its issues are denied.
Pull requests read refusal means the repository or its PRs are denied.
Actions runs read refusal means the repository is not accessible or actions are denied.
Actions artifacts read refusal means the repository or its artifacts are denied.
Issue comment write requires step-up auth. Refused because mutation_class is refused in default policy.
PR review write requires step-up auth. Refused because mutation_class is refused in default policy.
Contents write is a credentialed_remote_mutation. Requires live auth which is refused in v1.
Refs update is a credentialed_remote_mutation. Requires live auth which is refused in v1.
Workflow rerun is classified as destructive_remote_mutation and refused in v0/v1.
Webhook receive is classified as destructive_remote_mutation and refused in v0/v1.
GitHub App installation inspect refusal means the installation is not accessible.
GitHub operation receipt with verdict=refused without a more specific refusal_code. Defaults to permission_missing.
Google Workspace operation requires a scope that is not granted. Direct scope missing.
Google Workspace operation requires a user subject (email identity) that is not present. Resource missing.
The requested scope is restricted and requires a security assessment. Treated as scope_missing since the scope is not granted at runtime.
Google Workspace domain operation requires a customer ID that is not present. Resource missing.
Domain-wide delegation requires authorization that is not granted. Auth failure.
Google Workspace mutation operations (gmail.send etc.) are refused in v1 default policy.
Google Workspace live network operations are refused in v1. Network is disabled.
Google Workspace operation receipt with verdict=refused without a more specific refusal_code. Defaults to permission_missing.
CI evidence verdict hold means evidence is present but some assertions are unverified. Not a full failure, but gating.
CI evidence verdict fail means evidence is missing, malformed, or contradictory. Release gate blocked.
Non-empty blocking_reasons array indicates a hold or fail verdict. Default mapped to ci_hold; individual reasons may be ci_fail if they represent hard failures.
surface_mappings.notes: Ambiguous: blocking_reasons can accompany either hold or fail. Context from verdict field disambiguates.

surface_mappings.rationale: Bash tool detects dangerous patterns (command substitution, inline execution, env injection). This is unsafe payload content.
Bash reroute detects a command that should use a governed tool instead (cat->read_file, grep->grep tool). Refused because the bash path lacks permission for that operation.
Supervisor terminates the invocation after exceeding the max runtime seconds budget.
Supervisor cancels the invocation. Resource budget (time, attention) exceeded.
Runtime tool execution result with status=blocked means the tool was blocked before execution. Default class is mutation_refused.
Runtime tool execution result with status=refused means the tool invocation was refused. Default class is mutation_refused.
Compiler candidate rejected by the validation matrix. Candidate failed to meet contract requirements.
Compiler candidate quarantined — not accepted but not fully rejected. Kept for analysis. Still a rejection for gating purposes.
Compiler counterexample or candidate assigned a failure_class. The contract validation step failed.
GitHub OAuth web flow, GitHub App user auth, and personal access token auth are deferred in v1. All live GitHub auth modes refused. Honest deferral per contract_v0.
surface_mappings.notes: 5 of 6 auth modes deferred. Only 'none' (unauthenticated) implemented.

surface_mappings.rationale: Google Workspace OAuth and service account auth modes are deferred in v1. Live network refused. Honest deferral per v1 readiness artifact.
surface_mappings.notes: 6 of 7 auth modes deferred. Dedicated v1_readiness artifact declares the deferral.

surface_mappings.rationale: MCP has 16 tool handlers but no transport server. Not reachable via any transport. Refused because transport is deferred.
A2A remote federation is refused by default (remote_federation_supported: false in schema). Local-only in v1.

Bridge refuses credential material (tokens, OAuth codes, JWT assertions) from crossing the surface boundary in v1. Credential material must never traverse the bridge. This is a hardening class for future vocabulary; no surface currently emits a distinct credential_material_refused code — it is covered by raw_secret_refused and the bridge security posture.

unmapped_known_codes.why_unmapped: Mapped to unsafe_payload as closest fit, but a dedicated redaction_refusal shared class may be warranted in future vocabulary versions since redaction violations are not payload injection — they are evidence contract violations.

Sensitive path blocking (identity/token files) is conceptually distinct from raw_path_refused. It is path-aware refusal rather than raw path injection. Future vocabulary may add a dedicated sensitive_path shared class.

ACP cancel() is a lifecycle method, not a refusal. The refusal vocabulary maps refusal outcomes; operation intent (cancel) is a different axis. May warrant a lifecycle_event class in future vocabulary versions.
Accepted status is not a refusal. The vocabulary maps only refusal-class outcomes.

strict_mode_behavior.strict_mode_note: Strict mode is advisory in v1. Unknown codes trigger a warning in evidence pipelines but do not fail validation. Missing rationale on a surface_mapping entry always fails validation. Strict mode can be enforced by downstream evidence processors that consume this vocabulary.

claim_boundaries: This vocabulary normalizes refusal codes across 10 surfaces into 29 shared classes. Domain schemas retain their original codes.
No live provider auth. No transport. This is a static normalization layer, not a runtime routing decision.
Content-light: no raw tokens, paths, secrets, prompts, or private file contents.
Unmapped codes are deliberately excluded. The vocabulary is not a superset of all possible codes — it is a curated shared classification.
Severity ranges are maximums. Individual refusal instances may have lower effective severity.
Cross-surface joinability of refusals is enabled by this vocabulary but downstream evidence processors must implement the join.
The vocabulary is append-only. New shared classes can be added; existing class_ids must not be removed.
Strict mode is advisory in v1. Downstream processors may enforce unknown code rejection independently.
